Agreement to run an initial benchmark and provide access to staging environment next week.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-03-12
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood CSM), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE); Lena Park, Omar Hassan, Priya Rao, Ben West (Granite)

Auto-summary: kickoff + onboarding. Action items captured at end.

[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): All right, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining the kickoff for the Redwood onboarding with Granite Analytics, I'm Avery, I'll run the intro. Uh, quick rollcall?
[00:12] Lena (Granite): Hey good afternoon, Lena here.
[00:14] Omar (Granite): Omar on the call.
[00:16] Priya (Granite): Priya here.
[00:18] Ben (Granite): Ben joining.
[00:20] Maya (Redwood): Maya here from CSM.
[00:22] Diego (Redwood): Diego, SE.
[00:24] Avery: Great. Objective for today: align on timeline, confirm security/network gating items, and agree pilot success criteria. We'll also cover who needs to do what. Should be about an hour.

[00:40] Lena: Quick context — we're migrating inference for our customer-facing feature to a managed/dedicated setup. Need predictable latency for small requests, and we have strict PCI-like controls for some data.
[00:52] Avery: Understood. Diego, do you want to run through the high-level technical flow?

[01:00] Diego: Yeah sure. So Redwood offers Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. From our previous threads, seems like you want Dedicated to start, possibly Private in future. For the Dedicated flow we'll need VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud — what cloud are you on?
[01:18] Omar: We're on AWS, us-east-1 primarily. We prefer VPC peering to start, maybe Transit Gateway later.
[01:26] Diego: Cool. For VPC we typically ask for a small CIDR allocation and a couple of ingress rules. We'll provide a terraform snippet if that's helpful, and a short runbook.
[01:37] Omar: Terraform snippet yes please, that will speed things up.

[01:45] Priya: On the security side, we need SAML SSO, RBAC mapped to our groups, and keys to be in our KMS — we can't have customer data keys managed by a third party. Any issues with that?
[01:58] Diego: We support SAML and SCIM for provisioning; RBAC can be mapped. For encryption at rest, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations under private deployment. For Dedicated we have options to bring your KMS in via key-wrapping — I'll sync with Infra to confirm exact flow and put the docs in the packet.
[02:18] Priya: Okay, that sounds reasonable. We just need the exact support matrix.

[02:30] Ben: On pilot scope — we want to test 3 models: a small embedding model for search, a mid-sized chat model for product suggestions, and a reranker. Can you support mixed workloads on Dedicated?
[02:43] Diego: Yep, multi-model workloads are common. We'll surface cost/latency profiles per model. Also note quantization can change latency/cost tradeoffs; for the pilot we recommend running the baseline unquantized then try a 4-bit profile if latency allows.
[02:58] Lena: For success criteria: p95 latency under 300ms for suggestion model, embedding throughput of 120 qps with <= 50ms median, and no data exfil incidents. Also we need cost estimates for both dev and production.
[03:15] Avery: We'll capture that. Maya, do you want to talk timeline and milestones?
[03:20] Maya: Sure — propose two sprints: Sprint 0 (week 1-2) is access + network + keys + staging perf; Sprint 1 (week 3-4) is pilot with 3 models and smoke tests; Sprint 2 (week 5-6) is optimizations and production roll gating. Can adjust based on your team's availability.
[03:39] Lena: That lines up with our CI/CD schedule. We have an internal release on April 15, so production roll by early April would be ideal.
[03:48] Maya: Noted. We'll accelerate where possible.

[04:05] Omar: A few nuts and bolts: IP allowlists, egress rules, and whether you require mutual TLS. We run strict egress so we need hostnames and IPs.
[04:18] Diego: We'll give an allowlist CIDR and FQDNs. Mutual TLS is optional for Dedicated; we can do mTLS if you want extra assurance — that does add a little setup time.
[04:31] Priya: mTLS probably not necessary for the pilot, but we will want it for production if possible. Also, audit logs and retention — what's the default?
[04:40] Maya: We provide request-level logs with a 30-day retention on the basic tier; enterprise packages allow longer retention and export to your SIEM. We'll include the policy doc.

[04:55] Ben: Question on SRE handoff — once pilot passes, what's the typical runbook for rolling to prod?
[05:01] Diego: We do a canary rollout with adjustable traffic weights, and Redwood Console will show token-level cost and latency. We'll help run two canary deployments and then flip traffic. For Dedicated we can also do capacity reservations.
[05:16] Avery: OK, let's walk through the checklist quickly. First: we need staging credentials and a small sample dataset (sanitized) so Diego can run perf tests. Second: SAML metadata and SCIM groups. Third: KMS details. Fourth: sign the dedicated contract / PO.
[05:34] Lena: On the contract: procurement is ready but needs the SAML/KMS answers before sign-off.
[05:40] Avery: Understood — we'll prioritize sending the security docs.

[06:00] Diego: For the perf test — ideal would be a 24-hour synthetic trace with your typical request distribution. If not available, give us logs or a seed set and we'll emulate. We'll run a p95 and median latency profile and cost per 1M tokens.
[06:18] Lena: We can provide a 6-hour trace this week.
[06:21] Diego: Perfect. Also wanted to flag one gotcha — embedding vector dims and batch sizes: if you have variable lengths, batching behavior may alter latency. We'll include batching knobs in the runbook.
[06:35] Ben: How do we monitor model regressions — e.g., quality drop after quant?
[06:40] Maya: Redwood Optimize can run prompt sets and track eval regressions; we'll set up an eval suite for your core flows. We'll add that to the pilot scope as an optional task.

[07:00] Priya: A question: for audit evidence, do you provide proof of key control and separation? And can we request an encrypted transit log?
[07:10] Diego: Yes, for Private we can show KMS access logs and key wrapping proofs; for Dedicated, we can provide attestations and exportable audit logs to your S3 or SIEM. I'll note to include sample artifacts.

[07:25] Omar: On networking again, how long does peering usually take on the Redwood side?
[07:29] Maya: Once we have Terraform and CIDRs, typical prep is 2-4 business days for Dedicated peering; provisioning the pool and linking to capacity can take a week depending on capacity reservations. We'll confirm exact timelines in the plan.

[08:00] Avery: Let's cover risks — biggest risk is SSO/KMS gating causing delays, second is model quality regression with quantization. Mitigations: iterate on SSO early, and run quality evals before any quant push.

[08:21] Lena: Sounds good. On billing, we need an estimate for the pilot so we can get temporary budget. Can you give a rough cost band now?
[08:29] Diego: Rough back-of-envelope: pilot small cluster ~ $Xk/mo, embedding workload cost depends on vector dims and QPS; we'll produce a spreadsheet with scenarios.
[08:40] Avery: We'll include three scenarios: minimal pilot, mid, and pre-prod.

[09:05] Ben: A small note, our legal wants to know data residency — we need EU-only storage for some customers. Is that supported?
[09:13] Maya: Yes, we can pin regions. For Dedicated we can provision in eu-west-1. Private on-prem also works if necessary. We'll include data residency options.

[09:35] Priya: Ok, last compliance note — do you keep PII in logs? We need an option to redact PII before logs leave our VPC.
[09:44] Diego: We support redaction hooks and can configure no-logs for specific routes; we'll annotate the runbook.

[10:05] Avery: Great. Any other questions?
[10:08] (short silence)
[10:12] Lena: Not right now. We'll take the action items.

[10:20] Maya: Recap of next steps: 1) Redwood sends onboarding packet and terraform snippets; 2) Granite shares SAML metadata, KMS vendor, and a 6-hour trace; 3) Diego will spin up perf tests; 4) Maya schedules weekly standups starting next Thursday.

[10:40] Ben: Confirm scheduling — next engineering sync 2025-03-19 15:00 UTC works for us.
[10:46] Maya: I'll send the invite.

[11:00] Avery: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the packet and action items.
[11:05] Diego: Thanks, bye.
[11:06] Lena: Thanks all.

Notes: occasional transcription errors: Redwood product names sometimes transcribed as redwood runtime or redwood console misspellings in initial notes. References to 'KV cache' heard as 'K-V cache' in one spot.

End of transcript.
